To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a broad spectrum of secondary metabolites accumulate at the site of injury in potato tubers, (2) the accumulation of these metabolites is qualitatively and sometimes quantitatively altered following infection of potato tubers by fungi and bacteria and (3) the metabolites that accumulate are toxic to the pathogens and may be involved in disease resistance.

a broad spectrum of secondary metabolites are found to be present in healthy, injured, and stressed potato tissue and that infection and stress qualitatiely and quantitatively affect these metabolites.
a and b solamirine, a and b chaconine, a solanine and solanidine, and rishitin, phytuberins and lubimin, accumulate in potato tubers in response to injury and disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of secondary plant metabolite accumulation in disease resistance of the tuber, and the potential danger to the consumer from these compounds.
the identification of compounds that may be involved in the mechanism of disease and stress resistance of potato tubers.
the accumulation of compounds that may play a role in disease resistance of the plant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
infection and stress qualitatiely and quantitatively alter the spectrum of secondary plant compounds in tuber tissue.
the potato is a very complex organism, and the accumulation of metabolites in the tuber is influenced by a variety of internal and external factors.
the accumulation of the secondary metabolites is not specific for the disease resistance mechanism of the potato.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a broad spectrum of secondary metabolites is found in healthy, stressed, and infected potato tuber tissue, and that the concentration and distribution of these compounds is qualitatively and/or quantitatively altered by infection and stress.
potato tuber tissue contains a complex array of secondary plant metabolities that are influenced by stress, injury, and infection in a manner that is qualitatively and/or quantitatively different.
the potato tuber contains a broad spectrum of secondary metabolites that can be induced by stress and infection to accumulate at sites of injury and infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the potato tuber is capable of synthesizing and storing a wide range of secondary plant metabolite compounds.
potato tubers are a rich source of secondary metabolites that accumulate in response to infection and stress.
there are many secondary metabolites in potato tissue that are not normally considered in studies of plant defense.
